metadata.title: IEA International Civic and Citizenship Education Study 2016 Assessment Framework

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This document is an assessment framework for ICCS 2016 rather than an empirical analysis paper. It describes the conceptual underpinning and the mapping of assessment domains to instruments (tests and questionnaires), but it does not report an analytic dataset, sampling weights, or replicate-weight procedures. For ICCS micro-data analyses, analysts should use the complex survey design information provided in the ICCS international database/user guide (typically including student sampling weights and replicate weights) to obtain population-representative estimates and correct standard errors under the clustered school design. Because this framework does not conduct model estimation, no specific weight variable (e.g., W_FSTUWT/TOTWGT) or replicate method (e.g., BRR/jackknife) is documented here.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This is a framework/assessment-design publication that does not estimate student-level predictive models or report PV-based achievement results. ICCS cognitive achievement is typically scaled using IRT and may use PVs in the international database, but this document does not specify any PV generation or combining procedure for an analysis. Missing-data handling is therefore not applicable to the framework itself because no analytic sample is constructed and no imputation/deletion strategy is evaluated.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Used for assessment design only: the framework does not define an analytic subsample or inclusion/exclusion criteria for an empirical dataset.

data.outcome_summary: This ICCS 2016 Assessment Framework sets out how civic and citizenship education is defined and operationalized for measurement in the second cycle of ICCS. It specifies content domains (e.g., civic society and systems, civic principles, civic participation, civic identities) and cognitive domains (knowing; reasoning and applying), and it also outlines affective-behavioral domains covering attitudes and engagement. The framework describes how assessment instruments (test items and questionnaires) map onto these domains, and it explains the described achievement scale used for reporting civic knowledge. It also positions ICCS 2016 as building on ICCS 2009 to support monitoring of change over time, including attention to emerging issues such as environmental sustainability and social media for civic engagement. Because this is not an empirical results paper, it does not report model performance metrics, benchmarks, or statistical effects.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This record is an assessment framework rather than an empirical study, so there is no ML training/evaluation, no analytic sample, and no reported PV or missing-data handling strategy. Consequently, fields that normally require empirical outputs (e.g., main_findings, performance metrics, country-level sample sizes) are intentionally empty because the document focuses on conceptual and instrument design. The sparse extraction is therefore due to the publication type (framework) rather than missing information in an analysis section.
